articles.title: Summer Observing Preparation and Checklist
articles.summary: This article emphasizes the importance of thorough preparation for amateur astronomy observing sessions, particularly for deep-sky viewing at dark-sky locations. It highlights the common issue of forgetting essential equipment and supplies, advocating for the use of comprehensive checklists as the most effective solution. The author shares excerpts from their personal observing checklist, covering telescopes, accessories, documents, clothing, support hardware, and provisions, while also providing a calendar of upcoming astronomical events for the San Jose Astronomical Association.

articles.title: It's Time to Look at Mars!
articles.summary: This article highlights the rare Mars opposition in June 2001, marking its closest approach since 1988, and provides detailed guidance for observers. It offers tips for viewing the Red Planet despite its low southern altitude, describes prominent surface features like polar caps and Syrtis Major visible through telescopes, and discusses methods for identifying features and even spotting its moons. The piece also briefly touches on the visibility of other planets during the same period.

articles.title: The Dark Of The Moon
articles.summary: This article, "The Dark Of The Moon," offers an alternative observing challenge for those unable to witness a total solar eclipse: spotting the very thin new crescent Moon soon after its new phase, specifically on the day after the eclipse when it reaches its greatest northern declination. It provides guidance for this challenging astronomical observation, emphasizing safety and ideal conditions, and briefly discusses the significance of new Moon sightings in the Islamic calendar and a historical note about Omar Khayyam.

articles.title: The Davis Star Show
articles.summary: The Davis Star Show is a free two-day astronomy and related sciences festival held on August 24-25 at the Veterans Memorial Center in Davis, California. It features an array of activities including talks by prominent astronomers, a trade show, exhibits, solar viewing, a planetarium, workshops, teacher training, and a large public star party. The organizers are seeking volunteers to bring telescopes for the expected 3000 attendees at the night star party.

articles.title: Santa Cruz Observing
articles.summary: The Santa Cruz Astronomy Club is inviting SJAA members to join their scheduled observing nights at Bonny Doon Airfield on June 16th and 23rd. Bonny Doon Airfield is private property, but the owner permits the club's use one or two nights monthly. Attendees should arrive around sunset and can find directions on the SCAC website, with club news available via their message center.

articles.title: Celestial Calendar June 2001
articles.summary: This article presents the Celestial Calendar for June 2001, detailing lunar phases, planetary positions (Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn) with their Right Ascension, Declination, Magnitude, and A.U., as well as astronomical twilight and sidereal time. It also outlines upcoming events for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), including a talk by NASA's Larry Lasher on the Pioneer missions, the unveiling of an observatory model for Evergreen College, and directions to Houge Park for star parties.

articles.title: SJAA Loaner Scope Status
articles.summary: This document provides an update on the status of the SJAA (San Jose Astronomical Association) Loaner Scope program, detailing which telescopes are currently available for members to borrow. It lists scopes available for immediate loan, those currently out on loan with their due dates, and scopes with extended loan periods. Members can contact Mike Koop to inquire about borrowing a scope or to be added to a waiting list.
